messages.subject: [rkward-users] RKWard 0.4.7 is released
messages.body_plain:
Hi all!

Version 0.4.7 of RKWard is now officially released. As usual, an annoucement 
is available on the homepage at http://rkward.sourceforge.net .

Many thanks go to all who contributed testing, feeback, translations, 
documentation, and of course plugins! We'd be nowhere near as far in RKWard 
development without all your work.

Regards
Thomas

than to just run it. On a debian based system (and hence on ubuntu),

should fetch everything that's needed. Let me know, if you run into any further
trouble.

Regards

messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward - Help] RE: php-Problem in 0.4.7
messages.body_plain:
Read and respond to this message at: 
https://sourceforge.net/forum/message.php?msg_id=4281280
By: tfry

Hi Ralf,

I don't think this is due to the missing option, but might be caused by a related
small bug (which does not cause the failure, here, though). Could you try locating
the installation directory of rkward (something like /usr/share/apps/rkward/,
where the exact path is distribution specific), then cd to phpfiles/, there,
copy "php.ini" to "php_ini". Does this help any?

If not, did you check that the path to the PHP binary is correct under
Settings->Configure RKWard->PHP backend?

Which version of PHP are you using?

Which exact error message do you get? "The support file XYZ could not be found..."
or "The PHP backend could not be started..."?

Regards
Thomas

messages.subject: [rkward-users] [rkward - Help] RE: php-Problem in 0.4.7
messages.body_plain:
Read and respond to this message at: 
https://sourceforge.net/forum/message.php?msg_id=4281298
By: tfry

Update:

I just found that it is likely a third kind of error: "There has been an error
XYZ while starting up the PHP backend...". With the current version of PHP4
in debian unstable, I can see this error, too. It's due to PHP producing some
warnings at startup that it should not. See
http://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=419802
and http://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=361789 . (Not sure, whether
other distributions besides debian are affected).

It works fine with php5-cli, here, so if you have that option, try installing
php5-cli, and changing the setting for the PHP binary to /usr/bin/PHP5
(or similar).

Regards
Thomas
